payments.title: Payments (Stripe)
payments.description: Connect your account to collect deposits and invoices straight to your bank

payments.connectNotEnabledTitle: Stripe Connect isn't enabled on your Stripe account yet
payments.connectNotEnabledBody: Stripe won't create connected accounts until the platform account signs up for Connect. It's a one-time, free signup that can only be done from the Stripe dashboard. Once it's done, come back here and press Connect Stripe again.
payments.accountMissing: The Stripe account we had on file no longer exists. We have unlinked it — press Connect Stripe again to create a new one.
payments.feesPaidByAccount: Stripe's fees come out of this account, not the platform's.
payments.feesPayerWrongTitle: This account predates the fee setup
payments.feesPayerWrongBody: Stripe's fees are being billed to the platform. Who pays them is fixed when the account is created and cannot be changed afterwards, so a new account has to be created. Get in touch before doing it so no received payments are lost.
payments.modeManualBody: You issue invoices the same way and mark them paid by hand. Connect Stripe whenever you like and your clients can pay from their portal.
payments.phoneNote: Your phone is the card reader. No hardware, no monthly fee.
payments.phoneNeedsConnect: Finish connecting your account above first. What gets created is a full Stripe account of your own, and that's the one you'll use on your phone.
payments.phoneStep1: Install the Stripe Dashboard app on your phone and sign in with the account you just connected.
payments.phoneStep2: Tap +, choose to charge a card, and enter the amount.
payments.phoneStep3: Choose Tap to Pay. Your client holds their card or phone against yours.
payments.phoneStep4: Paid. It takes Visa, Mastercard, Amex and Interac. You need an iPhone XS or later, or an Android with NFC.
payments.phoneMarkPaid: A payment taken in the Stripe app doesn't reach this system on its own. Open the invoice and mark it paid, or it will keep saying it's outstanding.
payments.phoneOfflinePin: Some Canadian cards need their PIN entered with the card inserted in a reader, and those can't be tapped. When one won't go through, send the invoice's payment link instead.

settings.inviteUserHint: No email is sent: the person signs up with this same address and their account links itself.

settings.publicLinkFixed: The system builds it from your business name and it doesn't change — your clients already have it. If you need a different one, write to us and we'll change it.
settings.billingIdentityHint: This prints in the header of every document you send. In Quebec the GST and QST numbers are mandatory on an invoice.
settings.estimateTermsPlaceholder: e.g. Prices are valid for 30 days. Any change of scope will be documented in writing.
settings.publicChannelBody: This link opens your public chat: the customer answers with buttons, and when they finish their request arrives ready to price. It works with no Meta approval and no per-message fee.
settings.noSlugYet: You don't have a public link yet. Set it up in {{menuEmpresa}}.
settings.howToUseStep1: In your WhatsApp Business automatic Greeting Message — the customer gets it the first time they write to you.
settings.howToUseStep2: In your Instagram or Facebook bio, and on the "Contact" button of your Google listing.
settings.howToUseStep3: As a QR code on your vehicles, job-site signs and business cards.
settings.directWhatsappBody: The WhatsApp Business API can't be switched on from here: Meta requires the business to complete its own verification. Once you have the three requirements below, this screen can connect it.
settings.directWhatsappReq1: A verified Meta Business Manager account in the business's name.
settings.directWhatsappReq2: A WhatsApp Business app created in the Meta Developer Console.
settings.directWhatsappReq3: A dedicated phone number, not already in use in the regular WhatsApp app.
settings.suggestedWelcomeText: Hi! 👋 Thanks for reaching out to {{business}}. Tell us what you need here, or start your estimate request straight away at this link: {{link}}
settings.pasteInWhatsapp: Paste it in WhatsApp Business → Business tools → Greeting message.
settings.holdbackPercentHint: Held back from each progress payment until the job is finished — 10% is standard in Quebec. Leave 0 if you don't use it.
settings.logoHint: Printed at the top of every estimate and invoice. PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG.
settings.publicLinkBody: Anyone with this link can write to you without creating an account — ideal for social media, your Instagram bio, or your WhatsApp Business greeting message.
settings.estimateSections: What to include on the estimate the client sees
settings.showMaterials: List of materials to be used
settings.showMaterialsHint: Built from the estimate's own material lines, so it can never promise something the price doesn't cover.
settings.showScheduleHint: Built from the work projection. Knowing when it starts and how long it takes is what reassures a client most before signing.
settings.provinceHint: This is where every invoice's tax comes from. Pick where you file.
settings.holdbackTooHigh: Careful: at {{percent}} % you withhold that share of every progress payment, so your invoices will charge far less than the work is worth. In Quebec the holdback is 10 %.
settings.ccqSubject: My work falls under the CCQ (loi R-20)
settings.ccqSubjectHint: Almost all construction in Quebec does. If you tick this, you have to send the CCQ monthly report by the 15th of each month — even for a month with no work.
settings.ccqEmployerNumberHint: The one they gave you when you registered. It appears on every monthly report you send.
settings.countryHint: This decides which tax details you're asked for and which rules apply to you. Canada only for now — it's the one place whose rules we can do in full. If you're somewhere else, tell us and we'll add it.
settings.seesAllHint: Sees and does everything, same as you.
settings.seesSomeHint: Choose below what they can see. The rest doesn't show up when they sign in.
settings.pickAtLeastOne: Tick at least one area, or this person will see nothing when they sign in.
settings.areasHint: This is what you can grant or withhold from each person.

payroll.title: Payroll
payroll.description: What your crew costs, from the hours you approved. All optional: with no rate set, nobody appears.
payroll.noApprovedHours: No approved hours in this period. Approve them in {{menuCampo}} → {{menuFichaje}}.
payroll.noRateSet: No hourly rate. Set one on their record if you want to track what they cost.
payroll.noRuns: You have not issued any pay sheets yet.
payroll.rulesNote: These are the lines applied to every pay sheet. They come preloaded with the figures published for Quebec in 2026, but change them: rates move every January, and CNESST and the health services fund depend on your classification and your payroll size. Confirm them with Revenu Québec and the CRA before relying on them.
payroll.remittanceNote: What has to be remitted for the sheets issued in this period, grouped by who it goes to. Copy it into the matching form.
payroll.remittanceEmpty: You have issued no pay sheets in this period, so there is nothing to remit.
payroll.ytdNote: Annual ceilings are checked against what each person has already contributed this year, taken from the sheets you already issued. That is why a deduction stops in the exact period the ceiling is reached, and not before.
payroll.openingNote: If you started using the software mid-year, enter what each person had already accumulated. Without it the annual ceilings start from zero and you over-deduct for the rest of the year.
payroll.openingOnce: Entered once per person per year. After that nothing from outside is needed.
payroll.openingNothing: Nobody has a carry-in for this year.
payroll.annualNote: The whole year per person: what was issued here plus the carry-in. These are the figures a T4 and an RL-1 ask for.
payroll.annualNotAForm: The software does not file a T4 or an RL-1 — those are documents with their own boxes and their own process. What it does is hold every number they need, so nobody reopens another platform in December to find them.
payroll.adjustmentsHint: An advance, a bonus, expenses they paid, the tool they broke. Negative takes it off.
payroll.adjustmentBadAmount: One of the amounts is not a number.

paymentRequests.newTitle: Ask for a payment through the chat
paymentRequests.newNote: It reaches the client as a message with a pay button. Send it now or schedule it.
paymentRequests.sendOnHint: Leave empty to send it right now.
paymentRequests.empty: You have not asked for any payment through the chat yet.
paymentRequests.percentNeedsProject: A percentage needs a project — it has to be a percentage of something.
paymentRequests.needsStripeBody: A chat charge is a pay button, and without Stripe that button leads nowhere. In the meantime you can issue the invoice normally and send its PDF through the chat; the client pays however they do today and you mark it paid.

performance.overtimeExplainer: A shift is cut at the eighth hour of the day: before it is regular time, after it is overtime.

receivables.holdbackNote: There is also {{amount}} of holdback on invoices already paid. It is not overdue — it is collected when the job closes.

profitability.empty: No jobs with a contract or costs yet.
profitability.noLabourRates: Cost excludes labour: no pay rates are set for the workers.

accountingExport.title: Export for your accountant
accountingExport.note: The books in a file any accounting package imports. One file per kind, so the columns mean something.
accountingExport.failed: The file could not be generated. Try again.
accountingExport.columnsNote: GST and QST are in separate columns, which is how they are filed.
accountingExport.quickbooksNote: These two upload to QuickBooks as they are, without touching a single column. Upload them in this order: QuickBooks rejects an invoice for a customer it doesn't know yet.
accountingExport.quickbooksTaxNote: QuickBooks recalculates the tax using your province's code, so the totals come from its rules and not ours. If you renamed your tax codes in QuickBooks, you'll have to match them up during the import.

stripeBalance.title: Money at Stripe
stripeBalance.note: Where the money sits between the customer paying and the bank showing it.

datosEmpresa.title: Fill in my company details
datosEmpresa.p1: Go to {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuEmpresa}}. Two cards: your identity up top (name, RBQ licence, province and your public link), and below it what gets printed on every document.
datosEmpresa.p2: Fill in address, phone, GST number and QST number. That's what appears in the header of every estimate and every invoice.
datosEmpresa.p3: Further down you set your default deposit, your holdback (10% in Quebec) and the legal text that goes at the foot of your estimates.
datosEmpresa.nota: In Quebec, an invoice without GST and QST numbers comes straight back from your client's accountant. The banner at the top of the panel clears itself once you fill them in.

accesoTrabajador.title: Give a worker access
accesoTrabajador.p1: First add them: {{menuCampo}} → {{menuTecnicos}} → New technician, with their name, phone and trade.
accesoTrabajador.p2: On their card, press PWA code. A code appears.
accesoTrabajador.p3: Send it however you already talk. They open /campo on their phone, type the code, and they're in — no email, no password.
accesoTrabajador.nota: The code is shown once only. Generating another cancels the previous one — that's how you cut off access for someone who no longer works with you.

accesoCliente.title: Give a client access
accesoCliente.p1: {{menuCrm}} → open the client's record → Generate access code.
accesoCliente.p2: Copy it and send it. They go to /portal and type it in.
accesoCliente.p3: There they see their project's progress, their estimate, their invoices and a chat with you. They don't see your costs or your margins.
accesoCliente.nota: Generating a new code cancels the previous one.

idioma.title: Change the language
idioma.p1: Top right there's a languages icon. Español, English, français and italiano.
idioma.p2: It only changes your own panel. Everyone on your team can have theirs in their own, and documents come out in the language you generate them in.

conectarMcp.title: Connect Claude to Logiciel Construction MCP
conectarMcp.p1: Go to {{menuAjustes}} → MCP Conexiones AI and open the Claude card. You will find the MCP URL and OAuth Client ID there; use the Copy buttons and never share passwords or codes in chat.
conectarMcp.p2: In Claude, add a custom MCP connector and paste the URL and Client ID. When Claude opens Field, sign in with the authorized account's email and password, or use the worker code for a field worker or subcontractor.
conectarMcp.p3: Check the mcp:read permission, which is read-only, and press Authorize. Claude can only query information allowed by your role, project perimeter and company plan.
conectarMcp.p4: If you change roles, access changes automatically. To cut off a connection, return to this card and press Revoke connection.
conectarMcp.nota: The current phase does not allow Claude to create, edit or delete data.

rolesMcp.title: What each role can query with MCP
rolesMcp.p1: The administrator or owner can query the full view allowed by the plan: projects, operations, invoices, payments, expenses, profitability and QuickBooks audit. Office and accounting can query the operational or financial information assigned to them.
rolesMcp.p2: A project manager can query their projects and perimeter: schedule, work orders, tasks, team, documents and hours. A technician can query only their assigned work and their own records.
rolesMcp.p3: A field worker or subcontractor signs in with a code and can only query their projects, orders, tasks, schedule, hours and authorized documents. They cannot see financial information or other teammates' data.
rolesMcp.p4: Example: a project manager can ask “What pending orders are in my project?”; an administrator can ask “Which invoices are overdue?”. MCP always filters by company, role, perimeter and plan.
rolesMcp.nota: Every role is read-only in this first phase.

estadoMcp.title: What Claude's green status means
estadoMcp.p1: OAuth ready means Field has a valid Client ID registered so Claude can start authorization. It does not mean an active connection exists yet.
estadoMcp.p2: Connected means there is an active authorization for your company. You can revoke it from the Claude card; Claude will then stop querying Field.
estadoMcp.nota: The connection uses OAuth and PKCE; you never need to give your password to Claude.

misDatos.title: Where is my data and who sees it?
misDatos.p1: Stored, in Montreal, Canada: the database and the files do not move from there. While you work they also pass through the server that serves the software, which is in Frankfurt, Germany, and stores nothing. It is all written down in the privacy policy.
misDatos.p2: Four services see it and nothing else, each only its own part: the one that stores the database, Stripe when you take card payments, QuickBooks if you connect your accounting, and the service that sends the emails. It is not sold, not used for advertising and not used to train any model.
misDatos.p3: GPS position is stored only at the moment of clocking in or out, to know where the punch happened. There is no continuous tracking: between punches the system does not know where anyone is.
misDatos.nota: It is all written down, with names and addresses, in the privacy policy. The button below opens it.

nuevoContacto.title: Add a client by hand
nuevoContacto.p1: {{menuCrm}} → New contact. The name is enough; phone, email and address can wait.
nuevoContacto.p2: Creating them opens a message channel with you, so you can write to them from the start.

enlacePublico.title: My link for incoming requests
enlacePublico.p1: It's a chat anyone can open without signing up. Your address is your panel's, followed by /c/ and your link.
enlacePublico.p2: The bot asks a few questions — which service, what they want done, the address and how to reach them — and leaves you a draft estimate with it all filled in.
enlacePublico.p3: You change it in {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuEmpresa}}, in the Public link field.
enlacePublico.nota: If you change it, every link you've already handed out stops working: the QR on the truck, your bio, your WhatsApp greeting. Change it early or not at all.

queVeElCliente.title: What my client sees in their portal
queVeElCliente.p1: Open {{menuPortal}} from your menu: it's exactly what they see, so you can check it before handing over the code.
queVeElCliente.p2: They see the project's progress, their estimate as a PDF, their invoices, the photos you mark as visible, and a chat with you.
queVeElCliente.p3: They don't see your costs, your margins, your suppliers, or the estimate lines you marked as internal.

exportar.title: Export my data to Excel or PDF
exportar.p1: In {{menuCrm}}, the tabs across the top are your business tables: projects, jobs and billing.
exportar.p2: Each table sorts and filters, and you can hide the columns you don't care about.
exportar.p3: The download button gives it to you as Excel or PDF. The PDF comes out with your logo and company details in the header.

quePuedeHacerElCliente.title: What my client can do on their own
quePuedeHacerElCliente.p1: Accept and sign an estimate from their phone, approve or reject a change order, and pay their invoice by card. All of it without calling you.
quePuedeHacerElCliente.p2: They can also download their documents as PDFs, see the photos you marked as visible, and message you in the chat.
quePuedeHacerElCliente.p3: And they can say the work is finished. That doesn't close the project or take the last word away from you: it just tells you they're satisfied.
quePuedeHacerElCliente.nota: They can only accept an estimate you've actually sent. A draft you're still tuning can't be accepted behind your back.

crear.title: Build an estimate
crear.p1: Usually it's already started: whatever comes in through your public link shows up under Requests and estimates, with the client and description already filled in.
crear.p2: From scratch: New estimate → pick the client → Create estimate.
crear.p3: Then you add lines. Each line lives in a zone (Kitchen, Bathroom 2) and a category (Materials, Labour, Subcontractors). They save when you leave the field — there's no per-line save button.

visibilidad.title: Hide a line from the client
visibilidad.p1: Next to each line there's a checkbox. Ticked, the client sees it in their portal and on the PDF; unticked, they don't.
visibilidad.p2: It lets you break your real cost down for yourself — three kinds of screw, the helper's hours — and show them one clean line.
visibilidad.nota: The price doesn't change. What you hide is added up into a single line item, so what they read adds up to exactly what they'll pay.

margenYmerma.title: Margin and waste
margenYmerma.p1: They're in the panel on the right. Waste is the material lost to cuts, breakage and offcuts; margin is your cut.
margenYmerma.p2: Drag the sliders and the total recalculates immediately. Your defaults live in {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuMargenes}}.

enviarYaceptar.title: Send it and get it accepted
enviarYaceptar.p1: From the estimate you send it to their portal. It arrives with your logo, your RBQ licence and your tax numbers in the header.
enviarYaceptar.p2: They download it as a PDF and can sign it from their phone.
enviarYaceptar.p3: Once accepted, it turns into a project with its client, its dates and its work plan already inside.
enviarYaceptar.nota: They can only accept one you've marked as sent. A draft you're still tuning can't be accepted behind your back.

porFuera.title: Sending it by WhatsApp instead of through the system
porFuera.p1: You can, and with long-standing clients it's the normal thing: they're on WhatsApp and that's where they'll stay. First add them in {{menuCrm}}. A name is enough; you can leave email and phone empty.
porFuera.p2: Build the estimate in {{menuPresupuestos}} like any other and press Generate PDF. It downloads with your logo, your address, your RBQ licence and a number of its own, like EST-2026-0001. That file is what you send over WhatsApp.
porFuera.p3: So the system knows it's out the door, press “Approve and mark as sent” and choose “Approve without sending”. It's marked as sent without anything reaching the client here, because you already sent it yourself.
porFuera.p4: When they say yes, come back to the estimate and accept it yourself. That's what opens the project, puts the work on the calendar and issues the first invoice. Skip it and nothing at all happens: the estimate sits still and the project never comes into being.
porFuera.nota: Invoices download the same way, from {{menuFinanzas}} → {{menuFacturacion}}. And if they pay you in cash, by cheque or by transfer, “Mark as paid” is right there to record it.

crearOrden.title: Send someone a job
crearOrden.p1: {{menuCampo}} → {{menuOrdenes}} → New work order. Pick the project and write the title the way you'd say it to the person: "Tile the bathroom", not "carry on with the bathroom".
crearOrden.p2: Set the priority and who it goes to. It can stay unassigned if you don't know yet.
crearOrden.p3: The moment you assign it, it shows up in their field app without you having to tell them.

numeroDeObra.title: What Aa-26-0001 means
numeroDeObra.p1: It's that job's number. The capital is the project, the lowercase is the type of work, then the year and that year's running number.
numeroDeObra.p2: It's issued when the job is created and never changes, even if you later move the date or change the type.
numeroDeObra.p3: With that number, {{menuCampo}} → {{menuRegistro}} tells you who was there, how many hours, and how many are still unapproved.
numeroDeObra.nota: An appointment with no project attached carries no number, on purpose: it isn't project work. If you attach a project later, it takes a number then.

tiposDeTrabajo.title: Create my own job types
tiposDeTrabajo.p1: {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuTipos}}. Five come built in; if you invoice Toiture or Filage, create them with their own letter instead of lumping everything into "Other".
tiposDeTrabajo.p2: You can't delete one that has already classified work, nor change its letter: that letter sits inside numbers already issued.

comoFicha.title: How my crew clocks in
comoFicha.p1: They open /campo on their phone with their code, pick the project and press Check in.
comoFicha.p2: The phone asks for their location and it's required: that's what turns the entry into proof they were there.
comoFicha.p3: They mark whether the hours are billable and the type of work. When they're done, Check out.
comoFicha.nota: If they move site mid-shift, Switch project closes the previous entry and opens the new one in one go.

verHoras.title: See the hours on a project
verHoras.p1: {{menuCampo}} → {{menuRegistro}}: one line per job number, with the hours, how many people were on it, and how many hours are still unapproved.
verHoras.p2: If what you want is everyone's individual entries, that's in {{menuCampo}} → {{menuFichaje}}.

queVeElTrabajador.title: What my worker sees on their phone
queVeElTrabajador.p1: Three things and nothing else: what's on for today and this week, the clock-in button, and messages with you. On a job site nobody browses menus.
queVeElTrabajador.p2: They see the work orders assigned to them, with what needs doing and where.
queVeElTrabajador.p3: They don't see estimates, prices, margins, other clients, or their colleagues' work.
queVeElTrabajador.nota: They don't need to install anything. They open the address on their phone, type their code, and can add it to the home screen like an app.

acuerdo.title: Putting what you agreed with someone in writing
acuerdo.p1: In {{menuCampo}} → {{menuTecnicos}}, next to each person there's a button with a signature on it. Their agreement lives there: from when they work, until when, how much they earn and how often they're paid.
acuerdo.p2: Same for subcontractors, on their own screen. The difference is a subcontractor invoices you, so there's no vacation pay for them and the field simply isn't there.
acuerdo.p3: Leave the end date empty and it's open-ended. Whatever terms you type get printed word for word in the document, so put what you actually agreed there: who provides the tools, when overtime starts counting, how much notice there is.
acuerdo.p4: The agreement produces a PDF with your logo, your address and your RBQ licence. You can download it and send it however you like, or hand it over through the messaging so they sign it from their phone.
acuerdo.nota: A signed agreement can't be changed or deleted, on purpose: if you could touch it up afterwards, the signature would be worth nothing. If the terms change, you make a new one.

vacaciones.title: Planning someone's time off
vacaciones.p1: In {{menuCampo}} → {{menuVacaciones}} you pick the person, the reason and the dates. For a single day, leave the “until” field empty.
vacaciones.p2: The moment you save it, it appears in that person's calendar on their phone, with a notice on the days it covers. You don't have to tell them separately.
vacaciones.p3: And when you prepare payroll, the days away show up next to the hours worked. That way low hours explain themselves instead of sending you back through the timesheets.
vacaciones.nota: What you plan is approved straight away. What a worker asks for stays pending until you sign off, and until then they see it marked as pending on their phone.

ccq.title: The CCQ: what to record and where
ccq.p1: If your work falls under loi R-20 — almost all construction in Quebec does — every month you have to tell the CCQ who worked, in what trade, with what status, in which sector and region, how many hours and how much they were paid. It's due on the 15th of the following month, and it has to be filed even for a month with no work.
ccq.p2: Tick the box in {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuEmpresa}} and put your employer number there. It's asked once.
ccq.p3: Each person's trade, status, sector and region go on their work agreement, in {{menuTecnicos}}. There and not on their profile because it's what you agreed with them for that period: someone who changes trade signs a new agreement, and March's report has to keep saying what it was in March.
ccq.nota: The trade and status also print on the agreement they sign. They're what sets their collective-agreement rate, and whoever signs has a right to see what they're being paid on.

papeles.title: Each person's documents (T4, contracts)
papeles.p1: Every worker's and subcontractor's card has a **Documents** button. That's where you upload the contract you signed elsewhere, their T4, their RL-1 or a pay stub, and they sit beside their hours and their agreement instead of in an email nobody can find in March.
papeles.p2: Most of those come out of your payroll — QuickBooks Payroll, say — and can't be fetched automatically: there's no way to ask QuickBooks for them from outside. You upload the file, and that's it.
papeles.p3: By default the person sees them on their phone, folded under their day's work. That's half the point: the T4 goes out every February, gets lost, and in April they ask you again. If you'd rather keep one to yourself, untick the box when you upload it.
papeles.nota: A T4 has the social insurance number printed on it. These are stored privately and only the office and that person can see them, never a colleague. What we don't do is read the numbers inside the PDF: being right "almost always" about a figure that goes on a tax return is worse than not having it.

crearFactura.title: Issue an invoice
crearFactura.p1: {{menuFinanzas}} → {{menuFacturacion}} → New invoice. Pick the client, the project and the type: deposit, partial payment or final payment.
crearFactura.p2: You type the amount before tax. The system adds the tax.
crearFactura.p3: Before saving you see the breakdown: subtotal, tax and total.
crearFactura.nota: The number is assigned automatically. You don't type it and you can't change it.

impuestos.title: How the taxes are worked out
impuestos.p1: They come from the province set in {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuEmpresa}}. In Quebec, GST 5% and QST 9.975%.
impuestos.p2: They're worked out on the full value of the work, and each is rounded separately, because they're declared separately.
impuestos.p3: The holdback (10% in Quebec) comes off deposits and partial payments, never the final one: the final payment is exactly where the holdback is released.

numeroFactura.title: My invoice numbers
numeroFactura.p1: Format 2026-0001: the year plus a four-digit running number, per business, restarting every 1 January.
numeroFactura.p2: There are no gaps because an invoice is never deleted: voiding it marks it cancelled and the row keeps its number. An invoice missing from the series is the first thing an inspector asks about.

cobrar.title: Take card payments
cobrar.p1: {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuPagos}} → connect. You complete the sign-up with your own details and your bank.
cobrar.p2: The account is in your business's name and on your email, and the money goes straight to your account.
cobrar.p3: After that, your client pays their invoice from their portal.
cobrar.nota: If the platform is still in test mode, a real card won't go through no matter how complete your sign-up is. Ask whoever administers the installation.

contable.title: Get the data to my accountant
contable.p1: {{menuFinanzas}} → {{menuInformes}}. That's where receivables, profitability by project and the accountant export live.
contable.p2: You can also download any {{menuCrm}} table as Excel or as a PDF on your letterhead.

cobrarPorFuera.title: They paid me in cash or by transfer
cobrarPorFuera.p1: On the invoice you'll find “Mark as paid”. You pick how they paid you, the day, and optionally the cheque or transfer number so you can recognise it later.
cobrarPorFuera.p2: Exactly the same thing happens as if they'd paid by card: the invoice is settled, it counts towards the collected figure up top, and it shows in the accountant's report with the payment method recorded.
cobrarPorFuera.p3: And if it was the project's final invoice, marking it paid is what closes the project. That's why recording it matters even though the money is already in your account.
cobrarPorFuera.nota: “Card” can't be chosen by hand: Stripe writes that one when there's a real charge behind it. That way the report can't claim you took a card payment for something you were paid in cash.

quickbooks.title: What goes to QuickBooks on its own
quickbooks.p1: You connect it once, in {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuQuickBooks}}. After that there is nothing to press: what you issue here shows up there by itself, in the background, with no waiting.
quickbooks.p2: That covers the client, the estimate, the invoice, the credit note, the payment —card or the cash one you recorded by hand— and the expense. Each one as soon as you issue or record it, and the payment is attached to its invoice, so it stops sitting there as unpaid.
quickbooks.p3: Work agreements don't go: an agreement isn't an accounting document. Payroll does, but as a **journal entry**, not as QuickBooks payroll — that's a separate paid product of theirs you can't write to from outside. **And if you already use QuickBooks Payroll, say so on its screen**: then we don't send the entry, because it writes its own and wages would be counted twice.
quickbooks.p4: It also reads back. If your accountant changes an amount, a date or an invoice's status over there, the change comes back here and you see it in {{menuFacturacion}}, so you never end up with two different truths.
quickbooks.nota: Every invoice shows the state of its sync. If it says it failed, the retry button is right there.

quickbooksFalla.title: Something didn't reach QuickBooks
quickbooksFalla.p1: {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuQuickBooks}} lists whatever didn't make it, with the reason in plain words: usually a missing tax code that can be used on a sale, or a missing account in their chart of accounts.
quickbooksFalla.p2: Each row has its own retry, and there is one at the top that sends them all. That one goes one at a time on purpose: an invoice can't be uploaded before its client, and twenty calls at once is how Intuit starts throttling you.
quickbooksFalla.p3: Something not arriving breaks nothing here. The document exists, the client sees it, you can get paid. QuickBooks is the destination, not the permission.
quickbooksFalla.nota: If a retry fails again, open that row's technical detail and send it to us. It holds QuickBooks's own words, which is what's needed to fix it.

comisionStripe.title: The Stripe fee and where to see it
comisionStripe.p1: When a client pays by card, Stripe keeps its fee before depositing the rest. A $5,000 invoice doesn't leave $5,000 in your account, and that isn't a fault: it's what card payments cost.
comisionStripe.p2: On the invoice, under "card", it tells you how much Stripe took and how much actually reached you. The figure comes from your own Stripe account's ledger, not from a rate typed in by hand, so it's exact even when a foreign card pays and carries a surcharge.
comisionStripe.p3: Part of that fee is GST and QST, because Stripe is billing you for a service. That tax isn't a cost of yours: you claim it back on your return. That's why it's stated separately, and why it goes to QuickBooks split out, as a bank charge with its tax broken down.
comisionStripe.nota: It takes a few minutes to appear: Stripe settles the transaction after charging. Until then the invoice says the fee is still to be confirmed, and it fills itself in the next time you open invoicing.

costos.title: Spent, planned, and what's left
costos.p1: In {{menuProyectos}} → Cost tracking, each job has five columns: **budgeted**, **spent**, **planned**, what's **left**, and the deviation. Budgeted comes from the estimate the client accepted, plus approved change orders.
costos.p2: What separates spent from planned is the expense's date. A material order due in two weeks, or a subcontractor paid on completion, is recorded with its date and counts as **planned**: the money is committed but still in your bank. When the day arrives it moves to spent on its own.
costos.p3: What's left is the budget minus both. It's the figure you decide an extra by, which is why it also subtracts what's planned: if you've already promised that money, you don't have it even though it hasn't gone out.
costos.nota: An expense is corrected with the pencil on its row — no need to delete and retype it. One warning: if it already went to QuickBooks, the purchase over there doesn't correct itself; fix it in QuickBooks too.

impuestoQuickBooks.title: QuickBooks says your province's tax is missing
impuestoQuickBooks.p1: Your QuickBooks has tax codes, but none for your province. The invoice is not sent, and that is deliberate: sending it with another province's tax would be accepted by QuickBooks, and you would end up with a Quebec job charged at Ontario's 13% in your books with nothing to warn you.
impuestoQuickBooks.p2: You create it in QuickBooks, not here. In their menu: Taxes → Sales tax → Manage sales tax → Add tax, and pick your province. For Quebec it creates both at once: GST at 5% and QST at 9.975%.
impuestoQuickBooks.p3: If it will not let you pick Quebec, it is because the company is registered there under another province. Change it in QuickBooks: gear ⚙ → Account and settings → Company → Address, save, and go back to the tax screen.
impuestoQuickBooks.p4: Once it exists, come back to {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuQuickBooks}} and hit retry. Whatever did not arrive goes on its own, now with the right tax. No invoice has to be redone.
impuestoQuickBooks.nota: We do not create tax codes in your QuickBooks, and it is not laziness: they are tied to your GST and QST numbers and to the agencies you remit to. Creating a QST code for someone not yet registered would be helping them charge a tax they cannot remit.

tasasEnCero.title: Some payroll rates are sitting at 0%
tasasEnCero.p1: They are at zero on purpose, and it is always the same three: income tax withheld at source, the CNESST and the FSS. The rest — RRQ, RQAP, EI and their employer shares — come preloaded with the published Quebec figures and do calculate from day one.
tasasEnCero.p2: They are at zero because **nobody outside your company can know them**. The tax withheld comes from the TP-1015.3-V and from the TD1 each person signs, so it changes from one to the next. The CNESST depends on your classification unit. And the FSS depends on your total payroll and your sector.
tasasEnCero.p3: A zero does not break payroll: it still runs and every other line calculates. What happens is that line deducts nothing, so the net comes out higher than it really will be, and the difference gets claimed from you later. That is why it is one of the first things to set.
tasasEnCero.p4: You set them in {{menuNominas}}, on the rules tab: each line has its percentage field and, underneath, a note saying where that number comes from. The withheld tax comes from your accountant or the Revenu Québec table; your CNESST rate is on your annual assessment notice; the FSS one comes from Revenu Québec based on your payroll.
tasasEnCero.nota: The others are not forever either: Quebec rates are updated every January. Each line carries which year its figure is from, so it can be checked instead of trusted.

cobrarConElMovil.title: Taking card payments with your phone, no terminal
cobrarConElMovil.p1: {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuPagos}} → connect, if you haven't already. The Stripe account this creates is yours and has its own login — that alone gives you a card reader.
cobrarConElMovil.p2: Install the Stripe Dashboard app on your phone and sign in with that account. Tap +, choose to charge a card, enter the amount and choose Tap to Pay.
cobrarConElMovil.p3: Your client holds their card or phone against yours and it's paid. It takes Visa, Mastercard, Amex and Interac. You need an iPhone XS or later, or an Android with NFC.
cobrarConElMovil.p4: Some Canadian cards need their PIN entered with the card inserted in a reader, and those won't work by tapping. When that happens, send the invoice's payment link and the problem is over.
cobrarConElMovil.nota: What you charge in the Stripe app doesn't reach this system on its own: open the invoice and mark it paid, or your books won't match.

noVeObras.title: My worker sees no projects when clocking in
noVeObras.p1: Only open projects show up for them. If the project is paused or closed, it won't appear.
noVeObras.p2: Check in {{menuProyectos}} that the project exists and what state it's in.
noVeObras.nota: It may also be that the code you gave them is no longer valid, because another was generated afterwards. Generate a fresh one from their card in {{menuTecnicos}}.

horasEnCero.title: A job that was done shows zero hours
horasEnCero.p1: The entry was made against the project alone, without picking the day's job. Those hours exist and show up in {{menuFichaje}}, but they aren't charged to any job number.
horasEnCero.p2: For them to count, the worker has to clock in with the job selected. They aren't attributed to a job nobody picked.

noSeCobra.title: It won't let me take payment
noSeCobra.p1: Check {{menuAjustes}} → {{menuPagos}}. If the sign-up is half done, you can't take payment yet: it has to be finished.
noSeCobra.p2: If the platform is in test mode, no real card will go through however complete your sign-up is. That's changed by whoever administers the installation.

noLlegaCorreo.title: My client isn't getting any email
noLlegaCorreo.p1: Email sending isn't configured yet on this installation.
noLlegaCorreo.p2: In the meantime, anything you need to get to them goes through their portal and the chat. Both work.

avisoDeFallo.title: I got a notice saying something failed
avisoDeFallo.p1: First: you haven't lost anything. The notice appears when a request didn't get through or came back wrong, and what you had typed is still on screen. Hit "Try again" before anything else.
avisoDeFallo.p2: If it says your session expired, sign in again and you're back where you were. If it says the fault is ours, it really is: wait a moment and retry, because it's almost always a bad moment on the server and it clears by itself.
avisoDeFallo.p3: If it comes back, open "Show technical detail" on the notice itself and send us that line. It holds what the server answered, and it's the only thing that lets us know what happened without guessing.
avisoDeFallo.nota: The notice will never show you a bare code or a sentence in a language you didn't pick. If you see one, that's a bug on our side and we want to hear about it too.

borrar.title: Deleting things, and what won't delete
borrar.p1: Almost everything deletes from its own screen: clients and estimates have a bin, so do people and pay sheets. If you can't see the button, that screen doesn't have it yet and we want to hear about it.
borrar.p2: Some things the system refuses to delete, and tells you why. A client with invoices won't delete, because deleting would take those invoices with it — and an issued invoice is never deleted: it would leave a hole in the sequential numbering, which is the first thing an inspector looks at. Same with someone who has logged hours: those hours are the cost of a job you've already billed.
borrar.p3: To correct an invoice there's the credit note, not deletion. Both stay in the books, which is how a year has to be reconstructable months later.
borrar.nota: If a client asks you to delete their data and it won't because they have invoices, write to us: there's a legal obligation behind that and there's a way to handle it without breaking the accounting.

mandoPresupuesto.title: …I send an estimate
mandoPresupuesto.p1: Three things happen at once, by themselves: the estimate is marked as sent, it shows up in your client's portal, and they get an email with the PDF attached.
mandoPresupuesto.p2: The email goes out in your name, with your logo, and if your client replies it comes to you, not to us.
mandoPresupuesto.p3: From that moment your client can accept it and sign it from their phone.
mandoPresupuesto.nota: If your client has no email on file, the estimate still goes to their portal. The only thing missing is the email. Add their email in the CRM and they'll get it next time.

aceptaPresupuesto.title: …the client accepts the estimate
aceptaPresupuesto.p1: It turns into a project. You don't have to create it: it's born with its client, its dates and its payment plan already in place.
aceptaPresupuesto.p2: If your payment plan has a stage billed on acceptance — usually the deposit — that invoice is issued by itself right then.
aceptaPresupuesto.p3: And because an invoice is issued, your client gets the invoice email. One action on their side, everything else by itself.

emitoFactura.title: …I issue an invoice
emitoFactura.p1: It gets its running number, shows up in your client's portal, and they get an email with the amount, the due date and a button to pay.
emitoFactura.p2: It doesn't matter how it was issued: by hand, because the project reached a payment stage, or because you had a scheduled charge. The notice always goes out.
emitoFactura.p3: The button takes them to their portal, not straight to the payment page. That way it works even if the payment link has expired or you haven't turned on card payments yet.
emitoFactura.nota: If the email fails, the invoice still exists. An invoice is never lost because an email didn't go out.

pagaCliente.title: …the client pays
pagaCliente.p1: The money goes straight to your bank account, it doesn't pass through us. The invoice marks itself as paid, without you touching it.
pagaCliente.p2: If it was the project's final invoice, the project moves to completed. It closes by itself because nothing is left outstanding.

doyCodigoCliente.title: …I give a client a code
doyCodigoCliente.p1: The code appears on screen for you to copy, and it also reaches them by email with the link to their portal and an explanation of what they'll find inside.
doyCodigoCliente.p2: With that code they get in without creating an account and without remembering a password.
doyCodigoCliente.p3: The previous code stops working right then. There's only one valid code per client at a time.
doyCodigoCliente.nota: That's also how you cut off someone's access: generate another code and don't give it to them.

fichaTrabajador.title: …a worker clocks in
fichaTrabajador.p1: The time and the exact place they were standing are saved. That's what turns the entry into proof rather than a note.
fichaTrabajador.p2: If it was the first entry on that project, the project moves by itself from planning to in progress. People are working now, so it says so.
fichaTrabajador.p3: Their hours are added to that job's number, and you see them in the work log. If they clocked in without picking a job, the hours exist but aren't charged to any number.

cierroOrden.title: …I close a work order
cierroOrden.p1: If it was the last one open on that project, the project moves by itself to confirmed: the work is done.
cierroOrden.p2: And if your payment plan bills something on confirmation, that invoice is issued by itself and your client gets their email.

mandoAcuerdo.title: …I send a worker an agreement
mandoAcuerdo.p1: The agreement lands in their conversation as a document they can open, and the moment they go into the field app a notice appears right at the top saying something is waiting for their signature.
mandoAcuerdo.p2: That notice is only there while something is unsigned. The moment they sign, it disappears on its own and stops bothering them.
mandoAcuerdo.p3: When they sign, their name, the exact time and where they did it from are all stored, and the PDF starts carrying it printed on it. That's what makes the paper worth something if there's ever a dispute.
mandoAcuerdo.nota: If it tells you they have no conversation open, start one from {{menuCrm}} or from the messaging and send it again. A worker's conversation begins when the office writes to them, not when you add them.

emitoConQuickBooks.title: …I issue something with QuickBooks connected
emitoConQuickBooks.p1: Everything normal happens —its number, the client portal, the email— and it also heads to QuickBooks behind the scenes. You don't wait and the screen doesn't change.
emitoConQuickBooks.p2: It goes in order: the client first if it wasn't there yet, then the document. A payment attaches to its invoice, and a credit note to the invoice it corrects.
emitoConQuickBooks.p3: If QuickBooks rejects it you don't get an error in the middle of your work. It's recorded and shows up in the list of what didn't arrive, to look at when you can.
emitoConQuickBooks.nota: Sending twice doesn't duplicate anything. Each document stays paired with its counterpart there, so a retry updates it instead of creating another.

legal.privacyLead: What data is here, who sees it and what you can demand about it. Written to be read, not to cover me.
legal.termsLead: What this software is, what it is not, and what we expect of each other.
legal.signupNotice: By creating an account you accept the terms of use and the privacy policy.

privacy.title: Who is responsible for your data
body: **Christhian Paul Rodriguez Almarales**, a natural person, at Via Damiano Chiesa 1, 43036 Fidenza, Italia. There is no company behind this: I answer for it myself.
For anything about your data — knowing what I hold, correcting it, taking it with you or deleting it — write to **progetmanagement@gmail.com**. I answer, not a form.

privacy.title: What data is in here
body: **About the business using the service:** name, address, phone, email, licence number and tax numbers. These print on every estimate and invoice it issues, because Quebec law requires them.
**About its clients:** name, phone, email and job address. The contractor enters these, not us.

**About its workers and subcontractors:** name, phone, trade, hourly rate, logged hours and — when clocking in from the phone — the GPS position at that moment. If the contractor uploads them, also their own documents such as a contract or a T4.
**About what is invoiced and collected:** amounts, taxes, dates and payment method.

privacy.title: What they are used for
body: To make the software work, and nothing else. They are not sold, not rented, not used for advertising and not used to train any model.

GPS position is stored **only at the moment of clocking in or out**, so it can be said where the punch happened. There is no continuous tracking: the app does not know where anyone is between punches.
A worker never sees another worker's pay or rate. What each person earns is between them and the office.

privacy.title: Where they are
body: **Stored, in Canada.** The database and the files are hosted on Supabase, in its Montreal region (`ca-central-1`). That is where everything lives and it does not move from there.

**In use, they pass through Germany.** The server that serves the software is in Frankfurt. It stores nothing: it asks Montreal for what a screen or a PDF needs, and lets go of it when done. But while you work, the data passes through there, and that belongs in plain sight rather than in the fine print. Germany is under the European GDPR, which gives protection equivalent to what Quebec requires.
My being in Italy adds nothing to that: I administer the system from here, but there is no copy of your data on my computer.

privacy.title: Who else sees them
body: Only these, and only what each one needs:
**Supabase** — holds the database and the files. Montreal, Canada.
**Hostinger** — rents the server the software runs on. Frankfurt, Germany. It stores nothing; the data passes through while you work.
**Stripe** — processes card payments. It receives the amount and the payer's details; the card never passes through our server.
**Intuit (QuickBooks)** — only if the contractor connects their accounting. It then receives their clients, invoices, payments and expenses, which is exactly what goes in their books.
**Resend** — sends the system's emails. It receives the address and the content.
**OpenStreetMap** — draws the maps and turns an address into coordinates. It receives the address being looked up.
None of them receives anything for their own purposes.

privacy.title: How long they are kept
body: For as long as the business uses the service. If it stops and asks me, I delete everything of theirs.

With one exception that is not ours to make: **issued invoices are not deleted** while the law requires them to be kept. In Canada that is six years. That is why, when a client asks to have their data deleted and they have invoices, the system refuses and says so — write to me and we resolve it without breaking anyone's accounting.

privacy.title: Your rights
body: You can ask to **see** what exists about you, **correct** it, **take it with you** as a file, **delete** it, or **object** to its use. Write to progetmanagement@gmail.com and I answer within a month at most — usually within days.
If you are a worker at a company that uses this, start with your office: the data is theirs and they enter it. If they don't answer you, write to me anyway.

If you think I have not handled it properly, you can complain to the **Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec** if you are in Quebec, or to the **Garante per la protezione dei dati personali** in Italy.

privacy.title: What is stored in your browser
body: Your session, the language you picked and a couple of screen preferences. Nothing else.
**There are no advertising or tracking cookies**, ours or anyone's. That is also why you will not see a cookie banner: there is nothing to consent to.

privacy.title: If this changes
body: It will: the product is young. When something that matters changes, I tell the business by email before it takes effect, and the date above is updated.
The day there is a company behind this instead of a person, that will be said here too.

terms.title: What this is
body: Management software for construction businesses: estimates, jobs, hours, invoices, payments and the bookkeeping that comes out of them.
It is offered by **Christhian Paul Rodriguez Almarales**, a natural person, Via Damiano Chiesa 1, 43036 Fidenza, Italia. Contact: progetmanagement@gmail.com.

terms.title: What it is not
body: **It is not tax, accounting or legal advice.** The software calculates taxes and deductions using published rates and produces documents in the form Quebec requires, but it files nothing with any authority and replaces neither an accountant nor a lawyer.
Rates change every January and each business's own settings decide what gets printed. **Check the figures before relying on them.** Whoever signs a return is the one answerable for it.
The contracts and agreements it generates are internal management documents. They do not replace a contract reviewed by a lawyer.

terms.title: What you put in is yours
body: Your clients, your estimates, your invoices and your documents remain yours. I do not use them for anything other than running the service, and you can take them with you whenever you want: the tables export to Excel and PDF from within the software.
You are responsible for having the right to enter the data you enter — your clients' and your people's — and for telling them it is handled here.

terms.title: Collecting from your clients
body: If you turn on card payments, the money goes **straight to your own Stripe account**, not to mine. The payment relationship is between Stripe and you, under their terms and their fees.
The fee Stripe keeps from each payment is recorded on the invoice so you can see it, with the tax on top of it shown separately.

terms.title: Availability and failures
body: I do what I can to keep it up, but I promise no uptime percentage and compensate no outages. This is a young product with a single developer: I would rather tell you that than write a guarantee I could not keep.
If something fails, the software itself tells you in your language and offers to write to support. I am the one who answers.

terms.title: Stopping
body: Whenever you want and without explaining yourself. Export what is yours first, and tell me so I delete what is left.

On my side, I would only cut off access to someone using this for something illegal, or trying to break it or reach another business's data. With notice, unless notice is precisely the wrong thing to give.

terms.title: Governing law
body: Italian law applies, that being where the provider is. If you use the service as a consumer, this does not remove the protection your own country's law gives you.
For what is invoiced and declared in Quebec, Quebec law obviously governs — and the software is built to comply with it.

security.lostPhone: If you lose your phone you won't be able to get in on your own: write to support and we'll remove it after checking who you are. That's why it's worth setting up on a phone you use every day.

ccq.title: CCQ monthly report
ccq.description: What you have to type into the CCQ form, already totalled by week and by worker. It comes from the clock-ins; nothing to redo.
ccq.fixIt: Anything marked “missing” is filled in on that person's agreement, in their file. Without trade, status, sector and region, the CCQ won't accept the line.
ccq.noHours: No hours were clocked that month. You still have to file: the CCQ requires the report even with no work done, and the penalty for not sending it reaches 20%.
ccq.note: This is not sent to the CCQ: it's for you to copy into their form. Due on the 15th of the following month.

planes.estaEnEntreprisePrecio: This is part of the Entreprise plan, {{precio}} {{moneda}} a month. Field workers stay unlimited.
planes.estaEnEntreprise: This is part of the Entreprise plan.
planes.loActivamos: We turn it on the same day.
planes.asuntoCorreo: I want to switch on the Entreprise plan

nomina.cuerpo: This is where you pay the hours already clocked, produce T4s, and keep each person's agreement and paperwork — without retyping anything.

cumplimiento.titulo: The CCQ report isn't in your plan
cumplimiento.cuerpo: It builds your monthly report from the hours already in the system, week by week the way the CCQ asks for them, so you review it and file it on the 15th.

margen.titulo: Cost tracking isn't in your plan
margen.cuerpo: Shows what you've spent and what you've billed on each job, and how much margin is left. Today, not in March.

contabilidad.titulo: Connected accounting isn't in your plan
contabilidad.cuerpo: Sends your clients, invoices, credit notes, payments and expenses to QuickBooks on their own, and brings back whatever your accountant changes there.

reportes.cuerpo: Who owes you money and since when, which job actually leaves a margin, how much is sitting in Stripe, and everything ready for your accountant.

campo.cuerpo: Jobs, crew and clock-in are in every plan.

facturacion.cuerpo: Estimates, invoices and payments are in every plan.

equipo.titulo: Limited access isn't in your plan
equipo.cuerpo: Let in whoever you need with access to their part only: a foreman who sees the jobs and never sees the profit or anyone's pay.

instalar.entradilla: It opens like an app, without going through the browser. Nothing to download from any store.
instalar.iosPaso1: Tap Share, in the bar at the bottom.
instalar.iosPaso2: Scroll down and choose “Add to Home Screen”.
instalar.iosPaso3: Tap “Add”. The hard hat is now on your home screen.
instalar.iosOtro: You can't install from this browser. Open this same address in Safari and the notice will come back with the steps.
instalar.iosOtroPorque: This usually happens when the link is opened from inside WhatsApp.
instalar.androidOtro: Open the browser menu (the three dots) and choose “Install app” or “Add to Home screen”.

susc.entradilla: What you pay to use the system. Charging your own clients is a different thing and lives in Payments.
susc.sinPlan: You haven't chosen a plan yet
susc.impuestosAparte: That is the exact amount charged. Nothing is added at checkout.
susc.pruebaIncluida: 30-day trial. Nothing is charged until day 31, and you can cancel before that from right here.
susc.gestionarNota: This opens Stripe's page, where your invoices are also available to download.
susc.pruebaHasta: Trial until {{fecha}}. The first charge is that day.
susc.impagoAviso: The last charge didn't go through. Stripe retries for a few days; if you update the card now, you lose nothing. We are not going to shut the system on you over this.
susc.pagoExitoso: Done. Your plan is active — if you don't see it below yet, reload in a few seconds.
susc.pagoCancelado: Nothing was charged. You can try again whenever you want.
susc.noSePudo: Checkout couldn't be opened. Try again in a moment.
susc.stripeSinConfigurar: Payments aren't configured on this deployment yet. Write to us and we'll set it up.
susc.bloqueadoCuerpo: The rest of the system is on hold until you choose a plan. Nothing has been deleted: your projects, invoices and hours are still there, and they come back the moment you pay.
susc.bloqueadoDatos: And if you decide not to continue, you can still download everything of yours. It's yours, not ours.
susc.pruebaQuedan: You have {{dias}} days of trial left. When it ends, the system pauses until you choose a plan.
susc.pruebaUltimoDia: Today is the last day of the trial.

noSePuedeCobrar.stripe_sin_configurar: The system has no Stripe key configured, so there's nowhere to charge. That's on us: write to us from Help and we'll sort it out.
noSePuedeCobrar.precios_sin_crear: The prices haven't been created in this system's Stripe account. That's on us, not you: write to us from Help and we'll sort it out today.
noSePuedeCobrar.stripe_no_contesta: Stripe isn't answering right now. Nothing you did; try again in a few minutes.

mcpConex.entradilla: Connect Claude to the Logiciel Construction data your role and plan allow you to read.
mcpConex.seguroTitulo: Read-only, and revocable at any time
mcpConex.seguroCuerpo: Connections use OAuth and PKCE. Never share passwords or codes in a chat: authorisation is completed on the secure Logiciel Construction screen.
mcpConex.noCarga: The AI connections could not be loaded.
mcpConex.revocada: Connection revoked. That tool can no longer read Logiciel Construction.
mcpConex.noRevoca: The connection could not be revoked.
mcpConex.oauthListoQue: A valid OAuth Client ID is registered for this platform
mcpConex.conectadoQue: There is an active authorisation for this business
mcpConex.queSignifica: “OAuth ready” means we have a valid Client ID on file. “Connected” means an authorisation is already active for this business.
mcpConex.paso1: Open {{plataforma}} and add a custom MCP connector.
mcpConex.paso2: Copy the MCP URL and the Client ID shown below.
mcpConex.paso3: When {{plataforma}} opens Logiciel Construction, sign in as the owner or use the worker access code.
mcpConex.paso4: Check that it says “read-only” and press authorise.
mcpConex.sinClientId: There's no valid {{plataforma}} Client ID yet. Once one is registered it will appear here with its official callback.
mcpConex.pendientes: {{cuantos}} registration(s) need fixing: their callback doesn't belong to {{plataforma}}.
mcpConex.sinConexiones: There are no connections in this business yet.
mcpConex.caducada: Unused: it may already have been removed from Claude
mcpConex.noAvisan: If someone removes the connector from Claude, we get no notice. That’s why it’s worth checking when each was last used and cutting by hand what no longer belongs.

afiliado.entradilla: Recommend Logiciel Construction and earn for as long as the business you brought stays subscribed.
afiliado.sinEnlaceTitulo: You don't have a link yet
afiliado.sinEnlaceCuerpo: Links are issued one by one. If you'd like to recommend Logiciel Construction, write to us from Help and we'll set yours up with its agreement.
afiliado.comision: {{pct}}% of what each business you bring pays, for as long as they keep paying.
afiliado.sinFirmarCuerpo: Your link already works and records whoever you bring, but no commission accrues until the agreement is signed. Write to us from Help and we'll close it.
afiliado.suspendidoCuerpo: Your link still records whoever you bring, but commissions are paused. Write to us from Help to find out why.
afiliado.regla1: Credit goes to the first link that person clicked, if they sign up within 90 days.
afiliado.regla2: Commission is calculated on what the business actually pays, before tax.
afiliado.regla3: If that business cancels, the commission stops; if they come back, it resumes.
afiliado.regla4: You can't use your own link for your own business.
